name: New Teachers and AI
title: New Teachers and AI
answer: New teachers can use AI to produce plans and materials faster, easing the pressure of their first years, but planning is a skill that develops through doing it. A new teacher who relies entirely on AI drafts may never build the judgment experienced teachers have. Schools and mentors should therefore set expectations that keep some planning fully in the new teacher's own hands while teaching them to check and improve AI output.

sections.body: New teachers face enormous demands in their first years, and AI can help them produce plans and materials faster, which eases the pressure. The problem is that planning is a skill that develops through doing it, so a new teacher who relies entirely on AI drafts may not build the judgment that experienced teachers have. The idea is not to ban AI for beginners but to pair it with mentoring and clear expectations. A mentor reviews an AI generated plan with the new teacher, pointing out what works, what is wrong, and what should change for their students. That conversation teaches planning more effectively than either writing from scratch or accepting a draft, because the mentor models how an expert checks and improves AI output.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, mentors work alongside new teachers on AI generated plans, reviewing what works, what is wrong, and what should change for their students. The mentor's role is to model how an expert checks and improves AI output, so the new teacher learns to do the same. Schools can also set expectations for how new teachers use AI, for example by having a new teacher write some lessons fully on their own each month and use AI for others. Over time, the new teacher builds both skills. The goal is a teacher who can plan well with or without AI. The text does not give grade band variations for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or finding for this idea. It rests on practice and on the judgment of mentors rather than on research evidence.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The main risk is that a new teacher who relies entirely on AI drafts may not build the judgment that experienced teachers have, because planning skill develops through doing it. The text therefore sets a limit: new teachers should write some lessons fully on their own each month while using AI for others. The decisions that stay with people are the mentor's review of what works, what is wrong, and what should change for their students, and the school's expectations for how new teachers use AI. The goal is a teacher who can plan well with or without AI, not a teacher who depends on it.
